caption: There is no medical aid on this list and that's the part that keeps me up. What did you cut first?

slides.title:
How I spend
my R21 000
p/m salary
Living in Bloemfontein
slides.body:
Female, 34
Single mother, two boys (8 and 10)
Job: Legal secretary
Net salary: R21 000 p/m

slides.title: Rent
slides.body: The boys share a room. It's walking distance from their school, which is worth more to me than the extra room.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: Monthly shop plus the bread and milk runs
slides.body: Two primary school lunchboxes, five days a week. That's where it goes.

slides.title: School fees & aftercare
slides.includes: Fees R700 each, aftercare R650 each
slides.body: Aftercare isn't a nice-to-have. I finish at five and they finish at one.

slides.title: Car instalment
slides.body: Second hand, small, paid monthly. Without it the school run is two taxis and an hour.

slides.title: Takeaways
slides.includes: Friday chicken, and the nights I've got nothing left
slides.body: I tell myself it's once a month. It's closer to three.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Petrol & insurance, electricity & water, the kids' bits, phone & fibre, funeral policy, stokvel, clothing account, family support
slides.body: R5 500 of things I would struggle to cut. Most of it is for the children, not for me.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R21 000. That's about R26 a day for anything I didn't plan for. There's no medical aid here — every doctor visit and every chemist run comes out of this R800.

slides.title: I stopped guessing where it went
slides.body:
I uploaded three months of statements to Beyond Horizon and it sorted every transaction for me.

The school-related debit orders I'd never counted as one number came to R2 700.

No bank login needed.
